# Recipes — chaining with the Project Discovery toolset

Design source: [`docs/spec.md#6-chaining-reference-implementations`](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/spec.md#6-chaining-reference-implementations) — runnable verbatim; `pqscan` treats upstream output as input lines and needs no flag unless a format requires disambiguation.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph DISC["Discovery layer - compose, not rebuild"]
    S[subfinder - domains]
    N[naabu - host:port truth]
    M[masscan / zmap - internet port sweep]
  end
  subgraph PQ["pqscan - cipher-configuration plane"]
    P1["fast - 1 handshake"]
    P2["deep - 24-120 probes"]
    P3["pq - PQ ladder + verdicts"]
  end
  subgraph SINK["Downstream"]
    J[jq triage / diffs]
    U[nuclei - tls tags]
    R[CSV / WAL / CI gate]
  end
  S --> P1
  N --> P1
  M --> P1
  P1 --> P2
  P1 --> P3
  P2 --> J
  P3 --> U
  P3 --> R
```

## Domain discovery → cipher truth

```bash
subfinder -d example.com -silent | pqscan -mode fast -jsonl -o assets.jsonl
```

```bash
subfinder -d example.com -silent \
  | httpx -silent -no-color \
  | pqscan -jsonl -o assets.jsonl
```

(httpx emits `host:port` lines that parse unflagged; the `-from-httpx`
adapter for httpx `-csv` output — `url,status` lines — is landing with
[PQ-35](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/issues/80)'s flag wiring.)

## Port truth first

```bash
naabu -host -p 443,8443,465,993 -silent -iL domains.txt \
  | pqscan -jsonl
```

(naabu's `host:port` lines parse unflagged; `-from-naabu` covers its
bare-host + ports-block output once the wiring lands.)

## Internet scale (one shard of a four-box pass)

```bash
masscan -p 443 -iL cidrs.txt --rate=100000 --open-only -oX - \
  | pqscan -jsonl -o shard1.jsonl
```

(per box: split `cidrs.txt` operator-side today — `-shard 1/4`, `-ptr`
and `-rate 20000` land with the
[PQ-24](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/pull/90) and congestion lanes;
the deterministic shard core is already merged.)

## Estate PQ calendar job (who is not PQ-ready)

```bash
pqscan -l estate.txt -mode pq -jsonl \
  | jq -r 'select(.pq.verdict != "A+" and .pq.verdict != "A") | [.target.host, .pq.verdict, (.pq.reasons|join("; "))] | @tsv'
```

Weekly cadence makes the diff meaningful: `pqscan -mode pq -sorted -jsonl | diff yesterday.jsonl -`.

## Feed nuclei

```bash
pqscan -l assets.txt -mode fast -urls | nuclei -silent -tags tls
```

## Reverse-DNS workflow (IP ranges in, domains out)

Given an IP range, `-ptr` resolves PTR records with a pooled resolver and
promotes the PTR hostname to the SNI candidate (`-sni ptr-then-ip`):

```bash
pqscan -cidr 198.51.100.0/24 -ptr -sni ptr-then-ip -mode fast -jsonl
```

Bulk PTR enumeration at massive scale stays with massdns/zdns: pre-filter
there, hand the FQDNs to `pqscan`.

## PQ verdict view

```bash
pqscan -l targets.txt -jsonl -o assets.jsonl \
  | jq -c '{target:.target.host, group:.handshake.group_name, class:.handshake.group_class, score:.pq.score, label:.pq.label, hndl:.pq.hndl}'
```

## Crash-resume (the WAL journal)

```bash
pqscan -l targets.txt -o out.jsonl      # interrupted? the WAL holds what completed
pqscan -l targets.txt -o out.jsonl -resume   # re-scans only pending targets
```
